doc.title: Nancy Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Always a singer; choosing work over college
summary: She never decided to be a singer, would otherwise have gone into medicine, and left Central State after a semester because work was waiting.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: You’ve described yourself as a showoff.
Yeah. I don’t think it was – if you asked me, I performed, but I didn’t push it on anybody.
I’ve also heard you refer to yourself as a little ham at that time.
Oh, well, I knew – since everybody seemed to think that I had this little gift, I used it.
So when did you decide, I want to be a singer?
I never did decide to be a singer. I recalled always being one. I don’t recall deciding that I wanted to be a singer. I was always a singer.
You never went through the, I want to be a ballerina, I want to be a . . . ?

Nope. If I had not been a singer, I would have gone into something in medicine. I know that. But the voice was calling, and work was there. So it made it very difficult to think about going to Carnegie Tech instead of Central State. I stayed at Central State about – I think one semester. The dean was never able to understand why I did not come back, because I had a scholarship and all that. But work was already there. I’d already had a television show at 15.
